description: Copycat variants of the public ARC-AGI-3 games: each keeps one original game's rules and level-by-level progression exactly (the original class drives every step) and changes maps, colours, sprite art, HUD position and, where the game's code allows, tile size. Every level ships with a winning line proven in the engine and through arc_agi's offline loader.
review_rule: A copy is not a yardstick until a human (the Boss or Son) has played it and set reviewed to true. verified only means the stored line wins in the engine and the loader; it says nothing about whether the copy is fair, readable or the same difficulty.
held_out_test_copies: kept apart in datasets/test-only-games -- never train

out_of_scope.as66: test-only game, not one of the 25 public games

games.kept: Reaching Lurch's rules, unchanged: pick an arm, place it, the body re-centres on its arms; walls stop arms; hazard pools strike bodies on levels 2-4 (five strikes lose); outlines, decoy outlines, pellet eating and exact colour matching on levels 5-6; 60-click budget; same 6 levels in the same order with the same blobs, outlines and pellets.
games.changed: Every board transposed; new wall islands on every level and new hazard pools on levels 2-4, grown off the winning line (every arm and body of the line lands exactly where it did); decoy outlines and their keyhole marks moved; arms, level 1-4 bodies, keyhole marks and the strike / goal flashes redrawn on the same masks; click bar moved from the left column to the bottom row; all colours reassigned.
games.not_changed: Tile size: the board is already 64 cells at one pixel each (the camera's finest scale) and the body/arm maths is integer pixel arithmetic on 5-pixel sprites. Outline, pellet and level 5-6 body pixels are not redrawn: the rules read their colours and paint pellet pixels onto bodies. Real outlines and pellets stay where the transform puts them, and no wall or hazard is removed, so no level gets easier than the original (the stored line is the original's line, transposed).

games.not_changed: Tile size: the 3-pixel segment is a rule constant in the grow and turn arithmetic. Rods, dots and pins are not redrawn: the game reads rod colours and anchor pixels, regenerates rod pixels on every grow, and wins on exact dot/pin positions. Pins stay where the half turn puts them; the stored line is the original's line, turned.
